coding.note: Claims are deduplicated across the abstract and introductory contribution list. Mimi is coded TOK, so its codec-design ablations are NA; the separately claimed improved training tricks are TRAIN. The RQ-Transformer comparison is PARTIAL because adding a Depth Transformer changes model size. Main comparative results span Tables 2, 4, 7 and 8 (15-name cap). Comparator handling is MIXED: codec baselines are evaluated by the authors, while spoken-QA baseline scores are explicitly copied. No independent training-seed counts are stated; listener error bars and repeated generated samples are not training-run variance. Data disclosure is PARTIAL because the large unsupervised audio collection lacks reconstructible sources. H100 hardware is stated, but no training duration, GPU-hours or FLOPs.

claims.claim: Present Helium, a 7B text language model pretrained on 2.1T public English tokens.
claims.quote:
We present Helium, a 7B-parameter text LLM that we pretrain on 2.1T tokens of
  public English data.

claims.claim: Introduce Mimi, a neural audio tokenizer combining distilled semantic information with acoustic RVQ tokens.
claims.quote:
We train Mimi, a neural audio codec (Zeghidour et al., 2022; Défossez et al., 2023) that
  converts audio into the discrete tokens predicted by Moshi and back, using residual
  vector quantization (RVQ).

claims.claim: Introduce improved training tricks for Mimi's semantic-acoustic codec.
claims.quote: first level of acoustic tokens and introduce improved training tricks.
claims.ablation_quote:
This human evaluation shows a significant improve-
ment from using adversarial losses only, with a MUSHRA score of 81.0 against 58.8 when
using the mix of loss functions used in Encodec.

claims.claim: Introduce a hierarchical, streaming Moshi audio-language-model architecture supporting real-time generation.
claims.quote:
We propose Moshi, a new architecture for audio language modeling, which combines
  Helium with a smaller Transformer (Vaswani et al., 2017) model to predict audio to-
  kens in a hierarchical and streaming fashion.
claims.ablation_quote:
All models are initialized
with Helium and pretrained on audio. When not using RQ-Transformer, we predict the 8
levels of tokens with independent classification heads, following Copet et al. (2023).

claims.claim: Introduce joint multi-stream input/output audio modeling, removing explicit speaker turns and enabling full-duplex overlap and interruptions.
claims.quote:
We furthermore extend this ar-
  chitecture to model several audio streams in parallel, allowing for a conceptually and
  practically simple handling of full-duplex dialogues with arbitrary dynamics.

claims.claim: Introduce Inner Monologue: predict time-aligned text before audio to improve linguistic quality and factuality.
claims.quote:
we introduce Inner Monologue, a new training and inference setup
  for audio language models that significantly improves the factuality and linguistic
  quality of generated speech by predicting time-aligned text tokens before audio to-
  kens.
claims.ablation_quote:
All models are initialized with Helium, pretrained on audio and use
 the RQ-Transformer.

claims.claim: Derive streaming ASR and TTS by delaying aligned text relative to audio.
claims.quote:
we also show how forcing a delay between text and audio
  tokens allows deriving streaming ASR and streaming TTS from a Moshi model.

claims.claim: Evaluate Moshi components across text understanding, speech quality and spoken question answering, claiming state-of-the-art speech-text performance.
claims.quote:
We evaluate all components of Moshi along several axes, including text understanding,
  speech intelligibility and consistency, audio quality and spoken question answering.

claims.claim: Support several minutes of conversational context, demonstrated with five minutes.
claims.quote:
being streaming compatible and able to model several minutes of context (5 min in
  our experiments).

data_disclosure.quote:
We use an audio collection of 7 million hours, which we call the unsupervised audio dataset,
of readily available audio content, the majority of which contains English speech.

tokens_disclosed.quote:

  public English data.

rerun.quote:
RVQGAN produces tokens at 75Hz, so we only keep the first two
levels of RVQ to obtain a bitrate of 1.5kbps, closer to that of Mimi.
